dialogues.speaker: Patolichev
dialogues.text: Now, let's check the third batch of supplies. And while we're at it, let's also take a quick count of the medical supplies and ammo we have on hand... I hope we haven't forgotten anything?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'm also keeping track for you.

dialogues.speaker: Patolichev
dialogues.text: Heh, sorry about that. It's just that every time I get busy, I start talking to myself without even realizing it.

dialogues.speaker: Patolichev
dialogues.text: After all, any slip-up in the pre-op prep can cause the plan to fall apart entirely. I have no intention of dropping the ball.

dialogues.speaker: Patolichev
dialogues.text: Let me see... Oh dear, how did they mix up the column for weapon quality with the one for weight? No wonder the numbers don't match up... Ugh, now I have to start the inventory list all over again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (<color=#FFCC33FF>Illuga</color> looks like he has something to say...?)

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Patolichev, what's the status of the supplies going to Cliffwatch Camp?

dialogues.speaker: Patolichev
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you, Captain Illuga. We've had a couple of minor issues... but the first two batches of supplies are ready and can be sent out at any time.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Good. Judging by the look on your face, are the numbers in the reports and the inventory lists off again?

dialogues.speaker: Patolichev
dialogues.text: Haha, I'm dealing with the usual. You know how it is — once numbers are involved, everyone can't help but mess things up a little.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I appreciate all your effort. I'll also make sure I pay closer attention to the numbers in the reports I submit going forward.

dialogues.speaker: Patolichev
dialogues.text: Oh, please don't say that. I should be thanking you instead. Frankly, I've never really had to worry about the numbers for any strongholds you're responsible for.

dialogues.speaker: Patolichev
dialogues.text: If only everyone else took paperwork as seriously as you do. Why, my workload would be halved.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll leave you to it then.

dialogues.speaker: Patolichev
dialogues.text: Okay... Hold on, where was I just now...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It should be fine as long as nothing's missing from the inventory, right?

dialogues.speaker: Patolichev
dialogues.text: No, no, it's key that we get the numbers right too! We keep having to check every report again and again, precisely because no one takes number-keeping seriously.

dialogues.speaker: Patolichev
dialogues.text: But that's a problem we can't avoid, since there are so few Lightkeepers capable of handling paperwork.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you've been forced to check on-site.

dialogues.speaker: Patolichev
dialogues.text: That's right. But who knows how many more errors like this are still lurking in these reports?

dialogues.speaker: Patolichev
dialogues.text: Well, no point rushing things either way. I'll go through all these forms first, and then I'll head to the warehouse.
